ShaderNodeAddShader.node: Adds two shaders together so both effects happen at once. Use it to combine things like glow and shine.

inputs.Shader: A shader to use here. Plug in any shader node output.
inputs.Shader_001: A shader to use here. Plug in any shader node output.

ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion.node: Darkens spots where surfaces are close together, like corners and creases. Use it for dirt and grime masks.

inputs.Color: The color to tint the result with. White keeps the occlusion output as is; other colors tint it.
inputs.Distance: How far to look for nearby surfaces. Small values only darken tight corners; large values darken wide areas.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.

ShaderNodeAttribute.node: Reads a named piece of data stored on the object or mesh, such as a color or number, so the material can use it.

ShaderNodeBackground.node: Makes the world light up the whole scene with one color. Only use it in the World, not on objects.

inputs.Color: The color of the light coming from the world. Dark is a dim night; bright is a bright sky.
inputs.Strength: How bright the world light is. 0 is no light; 1 is normal; higher values light the scene more.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBevel.node: Fakes rounded edges by bending the shading near corners, so sharp edges catch light like real ones. Cycles only, and it can be slow.

inputs.Radius: How big the fake rounded edge is. Small is a sharp edge with a tiny highlight; large is a soft, round edge.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.

ShaderNodeBlackbody.node: Turns a temperature in Kelvin into the color of glowing hot things. Low is red-orange like embers, high is white-blue.

inputs.Temperature: Temperature in Kelvin. About 1000 is red; 6500 is white-ish daylight; 10000 and above is blue.

ShaderNodeBrightContrast.node: Makes a color lighter or darker, and pushes bright and dark parts further apart. Use it to quickly tune a texture.

inputs.Color: The color or image you want to adjust.
inputs.Bright: Makes the color lighter or darker. Negative is darker; 0 is no change; positive is lighter.
inputs.Contrast: Pushes lights and darks apart. Negative looks flat and gray; positive looks punchy and harsh.

ShaderNodeBsdfAnisotropic.node: Shiny, mirror-like surface like metal, which can also stretch its highlights in one direction, like brushed steel.

inputs.Color: The tint of the reflection. White gives a plain mirror look; colors tint it like gold or copper.
inputs.Roughness: How blurry the shine is. 0 is a sharp mirror; 1 is a very blurry, soft reflection.
inputs.Anisotropy: Stretches the highlight in one direction. 0 is round; near 1 or -1 makes long streaks, like brushed metal.
inputs.Rotation: Turns the stretched highlight around the surface. 0 to 1 is one full turn.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Tangent: Direction along the surface that the stretched highlight follows. Empty uses an automatic direction.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfDiffuse.node: A flat, matte surface that scatters light in all directions, like chalk or paper. The simplest 'not shiny' material.

inputs.Color: The color of the surface. Dark colors absorb light and look dark; bright colors look bright.
inputs.Roughness: How rough the matte surface is. 0 is smooth and even; 1 looks flatter and dustier, like clay or moon dust.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfGlass.node: Clear glass that bends light passing through and reflects at steep angles. Use it for windows, bottles and glasses.

inputs.Color: The tint of the glass. White is clear; colors tint the light that passes through.
inputs.Roughness: How frosted the glass is. 0 is perfectly clear; higher gets blurry like frosted glass.
inputs.IOR: Index of Refraction: how strongly light bends. 1 is no bend; glass is about 1.45; water is 1.33.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.
inputs.Thin Film Thickness: Thickness of a thin oily or soapy film on the surface, in nanometers. 0 is off; higher gives rainbow colors.
inputs.Thin Film IOR: Index of Refraction of the thin film layer. Changes the strength and color of the rainbow effect.

ShaderNodeBsdfHair.node: A shader for hair strands that shows shine and see-through glow. Older, simpler hair look than Principled Hair.

inputs.Color: The color of the hair.
inputs.Offset: Tilts the highlight along the hair strand, in radians. Moves where the shine appears.
inputs.RoughnessU: Blur of the shine along the hair strand. Low is a thin sharp line; high is soft and wide.
inputs.RoughnessV: Blur of the shine across the hair strand's width. Low is sharp; high is spread out.
inputs.Tangent: Direction the hair strand runs. Empty uses the strand's own direction.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfHairPrincipled.node: An easy, realistic shader for hair and fur. Set the color by melanin (natural dyes) or directly, then tune shine.

inputs.Color: Hair color, used when the parametrization is Direct Coloring. Dark is black hair; bright is blond or dyed.
inputs.Melanin: Amount of natural pigment. 0 is white or gray hair; 1 is very dark hair.
inputs.Melanin Redness: Mix of pigment types. Low is black or brown hair; high is red or ginger hair.
inputs.Tint: Dye color added on top of the natural hair color. White does nothing.
inputs.Absorption Coefficient: Sets how strongly each color is absorbed in the hair. Used in Absorption Coefficient mode for exact control.
inputs.Aspect Ratio: Squashes the hair cross-section from round to flat. Only used by the Huang model. Changes shine shape.
inputs.Roughness: How blurry the main shine is. Low is glossy and sharp; high is soft and dull.
inputs.Radial Roughness: Blur of the shine around the strand's width. Low gives a tight band; high spreads it across.
inputs.Coat: Adds a smooth shiny layer, like conditioner. 0 is none; 1 is very glossy.
inputs.IOR: How strongly light bends inside the hair. Hair is about 1.55. Affects shine strength and glow.
inputs.Offset: Tilts the highlights along the strand, in radians. Mimics scales on the hair surface.
inputs.Random Color: Randomly changes hair color per strand. 0 is all alike; 1 is lots of variety.
inputs.Random Roughness: Randomly changes shine blur per strand. 0 is all alike; higher looks more natural.
inputs.Random: A random number per strand, often from the Curves Info node. Drives the random color and roughness.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.
inputs.R lobe: Strength of the direct shine bounced off the hair surface. 0 removes it; 1 is normal. For Huang model.
inputs.TT lobe: Strength of light passing straight through the hair, giving back-glow. 0 removes it; 1 is normal.
inputs.TRT lobe: Strength of light that enters, bounces inside and leaves, giving a second tinted shine. 0 removes it.

ShaderNodeBsdfMetallic.node: A realistic metal shader using real metal data (IOR and Extinction) or simple colors. Use it for gold, steel, copper and more.

inputs.Base Color: The main color of the metal when looking straight at it. Gold is yellow; silver is near white.
inputs.Edge Tint: The color of the metal at steep angles near the edges. Usually a brighter, lighter version of the base color.
inputs.IOR: Real-metal data (per color) for how light bends in the metal. Used in Physical Conductor mode.
inputs.Extinction: Real-metal data for how fast each color is absorbed. Used in Physical Conductor mode with IOR.
inputs.Roughness: How blurry the metal reflection is. 0 is a polished mirror; 1 is dull and brushed.
inputs.Anisotropy: Stretches the highlight in one direction. 0 is round; near 1 or -1 makes long streaks, like brushed metal.
inputs.Rotation: Turns the stretched highlight around the surface. 0 to 1 is one full turn.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Tangent: Direction along the surface that the stretched highlight follows. Empty uses an automatic direction.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.
inputs.Thin Film Thickness: Thickness of a thin oily or soapy film on the surface, in nanometers. 0 is off; higher gives rainbow colors.
inputs.Thin Film IOR: Index of Refraction of the thin film layer. Changes the strength and color of the rainbow effect.

ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled.node: The all-in-one material node. One node can make plastic, metal, glass, skin and more by mixing its settings.

inputs.Base Color: The main color of the surface. For metals, it tints the reflection.
inputs.Metallic: 0 is a non-metal like plastic or wood; 1 is a pure metal. Use 0 or 1; avoid in-between values.
inputs.Roughness: How blurry the shine is. 0 is a mirror; 1 is fully matte and rough.
inputs.IOR: How strongly light bends and reflects on non-metals. Plastic is about 1.45; water 1.33; diamond 2.4.
inputs.Alpha: Opacity. 1 is solid; 0 is fully see-through; values between are partly transparent.
inputs.Thin Wall: On means a thin sheet like a soap bubble or leaf, so light is not bent inside. Off treats it as solid.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.
inputs.Diffuse Roughness: Roughness of the matte part. 0 is smooth; higher looks flatter and dustier, like clay.
inputs.Subsurface Weight: How much light scatters inside, like skin or wax. 0 is solid; 1 is fully soft and glowy.
inputs.Subsurface Radius: How far light travels inside for red, green and blue. Larger gives a softer, deeper look.
inputs.Subsurface Scale: Overall multiplier for the Radius. Small is a thin, tight glow; large spreads light deeper.
inputs.Subsurface IOR: How strongly light bends at the surface when scattering. Used in the Random Walk (Skin) method only.
inputs.Subsurface Anisotropy: Direction light scatters inside. Negative bounces back; 0 is even; positive pushes it forward.
inputs.Specular IOR Level: Strength of the shine on non-metals. 0 is no shine; 0.5 is normal; 1 is extra bright.
inputs.Specular Tint: Color that tints the shine at head-on angles. White is plain; other colors tint it.
inputs.Anisotropic: Stretches the highlight in one direction. 0 is round; 1 makes long streaks like brushed metal.
inputs.Anisotropic Rotation: Turns the stretched highlight around the surface. 0 to 1 is a full turn.
inputs.Tangent: Direction along the surface that the stretched highlight follows. Empty uses an automatic direction.
inputs.Transmission Weight: How see-through like glass the surface is. 0 is solid; 1 is fully glass.
inputs.Coat Weight: Adds a shiny clear layer on top, like car paint or lacquer. 0 is none; 1 is full coat.
inputs.Coat Roughness: How blurry the clear coat shine is. 0 is a sharp mirror; 1 is soft.
inputs.Coat IOR: How strongly light bends in the clear coat. About 1.5 for a normal varnish.
inputs.Coat Tint: Color of the clear coat layer. White is clear; colors tint like colored lacquer.
inputs.Coat Normal: Surface direction for the coat only. Lets the coat be smooth while the base is bumpy.
inputs.Sheen Weight: Adds a soft fuzzy glow at edges, like cloth. 0 is none; 1 is full.
inputs.Sheen Roughness: How wide the sheen glow spreads. Low is a thin tight rim; high is broad and soft.
inputs.Sheen Tint: Color of the sheen glow. White is plain; other colors tint the fuzz.
inputs.Emission Color: The color of the glow the surface gives off.
inputs.Emission Strength: How bright the glow is. 0 is off; 1 is normal; higher is brighter and lights nearby things.
inputs.Thin Film Thickness: Thickness of a thin oily or soapy film on the surface, in nanometers. 0 is off; higher gives rainbow colors.
inputs.Thin Film IOR: Index of Refraction of the thin film layer. Changes the strength and color of the rainbow effect.

ShaderNodeBsdfRayPortal.node: Makes light rays jump to a new place and direction, like a portal. Used for tricks such as fake windows or teleporting views.

inputs.Color: Tints the light passing through the portal. White passes light unchanged.
inputs.Position: The new place where the ray continues from, in world space.
inputs.Direction: The new direction the ray travels in after the portal.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfRefraction.node: Bends light as it passes into a see-through material, like glass without the mirror reflection. Mix it with Glossy yourself.

inputs.Color: The tint of the see-through material. White is clear; colors tint the light.
inputs.Roughness: How frosted it is. 0 is clear and sharp; higher gets blurry.
inputs.IOR: Index of Refraction: how strongly light bends. 1 is no bend; glass is about 1.45; water is 1.33.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfSheen.node: Adds the soft, fuzzy glow seen at the edges of cloth like velvet. Usually mixed with another shader.

inputs.Color: The color of the soft fuzzy glow at the edges.
inputs.Roughness: How wide the glow spreads. Low is a thin tight rim; high is broad and soft.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfToon.node: Gives light a cartoon look with hard color bands instead of smooth shading. Use it for cel-shaded art.

inputs.Color: The color of the surface. Dark colors absorb light and look dark; bright colors look bright.
inputs.Size: How big the bright cartoon area is. Small gives a tiny spot; large lights most of the surface.
inputs.Smooth: Softens the hard edge between light and dark. 0 is a sharp cartoon edge; higher blends smoothly.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfTranslucent.node: Lets light pass through a thin object and glow from the other side, like a leaf or lampshade. Not clear like glass.

inputs.Color: The color of the light that glows through. Dark blocks light; bright lets more through.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBsdfTransparent.node: Makes a surface fully see-through with no bending. Mix it with another shader to cut out shapes.

inputs.Color: Tints light passing through. White is fully clear; colors tint it; black blocks it.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeBump.node: Fakes small bumps from a grayscale height map without changing the real shape. Its output goes into a Normal input.

inputs.Strength: How strong the bumps look. 0 is flat; 1 is full bumps; values in between soften them.
inputs.Distance: How tall the bumps are in scene units. Small is shallow detail; large is deep, dramatic bumps.
inputs.Filter Width: How wide the area used to read the height is. Small is sharp; larger blurs and smooths bumps.
inputs.Height: A grayscale value or texture. White is high, black is low. This makes the bumps.
inputs.Normal: Base surface direction to add bumps to. Empty uses the real surface.

ShaderNodeCameraData.node: Gives facts about how far and in what direction a point is from the camera. Use it for distance fades and depth effects.

ShaderNodeClamp.node: Squeezes a number so it never goes below a minimum or above a maximum, like a ceiling and a floor.

inputs.Min: The lowest the result can be. Anything below it is raised to this.
inputs.Max: The highest the result can be. Anything above it is lowered to this.

ShaderNodeCombineColor.node: Builds one color from three separate numbers (like red, green, blue). Opposite of Separate Color.

inputs.Red: The red amount for the new color. 0 is none; 1 is full. (Name changes with the chosen color model.)
inputs.Green: The green amount for the new color. 0 is none; 1 is full. (Name changes with the chosen color model.)
inputs.Blue: The blue amount for the new color. 0 is none; 1 is full. (Name changes with the chosen color model.)

ShaderNodeCombineXYZ.node: Builds one vector (a point or direction) from three separate X, Y and Z numbers. Opposite of Separate XYZ.

inputs.X: The left-right part of the vector.
inputs.Y: The forward-back part of the vector.
inputs.Z: The up-down part of the vector.

ShaderNodeDisplacement.node: Pushes the surface in or out along its normal using a height value. Plug into Material Output Displacement for real bumps.

inputs.Height: How much to push the surface out. Higher values push farther along the normal.
inputs.Midlevel: The height value that means no movement. Below it pushes in; above it pushes out.
inputs.Scale: Overall multiplier for the push. 0 means no change; larger exaggerates the bumps.
inputs.Normal: The direction to push along. Empty uses the surface normal.

ShaderNodeEeveeSpecular.node: An older EEVEE-only material where you pick the shine color directly instead of using Metallic. Not used in Cycles.

inputs.Base Color: The main color of the surface (diffuse color).
inputs.Specular: The color and strength of the shine. Dark is no shine; bright is strong shine.
inputs.Roughness: How blurry the shine is. 0 is a sharp mirror; 1 is a very blurry, soft reflection.
inputs.Emissive Color: The color of light the surface gives off.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Clear Coat: Adds a shiny clear layer on top. 0 is none; 1 is full.
inputs.Clear Coat Roughness: Blur of the clear coat shine. 0 is a sharp mirror; 1 is soft.
inputs.Clear Coat Normal: Surface direction used only for the clear coat layer.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeEmission.node: Makes a surface glow and give off light, like a lamp or screen. Use it for lights, neon and glowing parts.

inputs.Color: The color of the light given off.
inputs.Strength: How bright the glow is. 0 is off; 1 is normal; higher is brighter.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeFloatCurve.node: Reshapes a number using a curve you draw. Plot input on one side and the new output on the other.

inputs.Factor: How much of the curve change to apply. 0 gives the original value; 1 gives the full curve result.
inputs.Value: The number to reshape. Its position on the curve decides the output.

ShaderNodeFresnel.node: Outputs more at steep, grazing angles and less when looking straight on. Real glass, water and varnish behave like this.

inputs.IOR: How strongly light bends. Higher means more reflection even head-on. Glass is about 1.45; water 1.33.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.

ShaderNodeGamma.node: Brightens or darkens the middle tones of a color while keeping pure black and white. Gamma above 1 brightens.

inputs.Color: The color to adjust.
inputs.Gamma: Changes the mid-tones. Below 1 is darker; 1 is no change; above 1 is brighter.

ShaderNodeHairInfo.node: Reads facts about a hair strand, like how far along it you are, its thickness and its random value. Use for hair color variation.

ShaderNodeHoldout.node: Cuts a see-through hole in the render, leaving transparent pixels. Useful for compositing objects into other images.

inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeHueSaturation.node: Changes the shade, color strength and brightness of a color. Use it to tint or recolor textures.

inputs.Hue: Shifts the color around the color wheel. 0.5 is no change; other values change the shade.
inputs.Saturation: How colorful it is. 0 is gray; 1 is normal; above 1 is extra vivid.
inputs.Value: How bright it is. 0 is black; 1 is normal; above 1 is brighter.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the effect is applied. 0 leaves the input unchanged; 1 applies the effect fully.
inputs.Color: The color or image you want to adjust.

ShaderNodeInvert.node: Flips a color to its opposite, like a photo negative. Black becomes white and red becomes cyan.

inputs.Fac: How strongly the effect is applied. 0 leaves the input unchanged; 1 applies the effect fully.
inputs.Color: The color to flip into its opposite.

ShaderNodeLayerWeight.node: Outputs a mask that changes between the center of an object and its edges. Good for rim effects.

inputs.Blend: Moves the line between the center and edge. Low shows mostly the edge; high shows mostly the center.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.

ShaderNodeLightFalloff.node: Changes how fast a light fades with distance. Useful for non-realistic lighting, since real light has fixed falloff.

inputs.Strength: The light brightness to adjust. Higher is brighter.
inputs.Smooth: Softens bright spots near the light. 0 is none; higher removes harsh hot spots close to it.

ShaderNodeLightPath.node: Tells the shader what kind of light ray is hitting it, such as camera or shadow. Use it to make things look different to rays.

ShaderNodeMapRange.node: Takes a number from one range and rescales it into another range, like turning 0 to 1 into 10 to 50.

inputs.From Min: The low end of the range you start from.
inputs.From Max: The high end of the range you start from.
inputs.To Min: The value the From Min end becomes.
inputs.To Max: The value the From Max end becomes.
inputs.Steps: Number of steps, used in Stepped mode. Low gives chunky bands; high gives fine ones.
inputs.Vector: The vector to remap, one value per axis.
inputs.From_Min_FLOAT3: The low end of the range you start from, per X, Y and Z.
inputs.From_Max_FLOAT3: The high end of the range you start from, per X, Y and Z.
inputs.To_Min_FLOAT3: The values that From Min becomes, per X, Y and Z.
inputs.To_Max_FLOAT3: The values that From Max becomes, per X, Y and Z.
inputs.Steps_FLOAT3: Number of steps per axis, used in Stepped mode. Low is chunky; high is fine.

ShaderNodeMapping.node: Moves, rotates and scales texture coordinates. Use it to place, tilt and resize a texture on an object.

inputs.Vector: The coordinates to change. Plug in Texture Coordinate. Empty uses the default position.
inputs.Location: Slides the pattern in X, Y and Z. 0 means no shift; larger values move it farther.
inputs.Rotation: Turns the pattern around X, Y and Z, in degrees.
inputs.Scale: Resizes the pattern. Above 1 makes the texture look smaller and repeat more; below 1 makes it bigger.

ShaderNodeMath.node: Does math on numbers, such as add, multiply, round or compare. Pick the operation from the drop-down.

inputs.Value: The first number for the math operation.
inputs.Value_001: The second number for the math operation. Hidden for one-input operations.
inputs.Value_002: The third number for the math operation. Only shown for three-input operations.

ShaderNodeMix.node: Blends two things (numbers, vectors, colors or rotations) by a factor. 0 gives A, 1 gives B.

inputs.Factor_Float: How much of B to mix in. 0 is all A; 1 is all B; 0.5 is half and half.
inputs.Factor_Vector: How much of B to mix in for each axis. 0 is all A; 1 is all B.
inputs.A_Float: The first number, shown when Factor is 0.
inputs.B_Float: The second number, shown when Factor is 1.
inputs.A_Vector: The first vector, shown when Factor is 0.
inputs.B_Vector: The second vector, shown when Factor is 1.
inputs.A_Color: The first color, shown when Factor is 0.
inputs.B_Color: The second color, shown when Factor is 1.
inputs.A_Rotation: The first rotation, shown when Factor is 0.
inputs.B_Rotation: The second rotation, shown when Factor is 1.

ShaderNodeMixRGB.node: Old color-mixing node. Blends two colors using a blend mode and a factor. Use the new Mix node for new work.

inputs.Fac: How much of Color2 to mix in. 0 is all Color1; 1 is all Color2.
inputs.Color1: The first color, or the base layer.
inputs.Color2: The second color, or the layer blended on top.

ShaderNodeMixShader.node: Blends two shaders together by a factor. 0 shows the first, 1 shows the second. Great for layering materials.

inputs.Fac: How much of the second shader to show. 0 is only the first; 1 is only the second; 0.5 is half each.
inputs.Shader: The first shader, shown when Factor is 0.
inputs.Shader_001: The second shader, shown when Factor is 1.

ShaderNodeNewGeometry.node: Gives raw facts about the surface point being shaded, such as its position, normal, and whether it is a back face.

ShaderNodeNormal.node: Gives you a direction vector you can set with a ball widget and shows how closely it matches the input direction.

inputs.Normal: The direction you want to compare against. Turn the ball to set it, or plug a vector in.

ShaderNodeNormalMap.node: Turns a blue-purple normal map image into fake surface detail. Plug its output into the Normal input of a shader.

inputs.Strength: How strong the fake detail looks. 0 is flat; 1 is full; higher exaggerates it.
inputs.Color: The normal map image. It looks blue-purple. Use Non-Color for the image's color space.

ShaderNodeObjectInfo.node: Reads facts about the object being shaded, such as its position and a random number unique per object.

ShaderNodeOutputAOV.node: Sends a custom color or number to its own render pass, which you can use later in compositing.

inputs.Color: A color to send out to the AOV render pass of the same name.
inputs.Value: A number to send out to the AOV render pass of the same name.

ShaderNodeOutputLight.node: The end of a light's node tree. Whatever you connect here decides how that light object shines.

inputs.Surface: The shader that decides how the light shines. Usually an Emission shader.

ShaderNodeOutputLineStyle.node: The end of a Freestyle line style tree. It controls the color and transparency of the drawn lines.

inputs.Color: The texture or color to mix into the line color.
inputs.Color Fac: How much of Color replaces the base line color. 0 keeps the base; 1 uses Color fully.
inputs.Alpha: The texture or value to mix into line transparency.
inputs.Alpha Fac: How much of Alpha replaces the base line opacity. 0 keeps the base; 1 uses Alpha fully.

ShaderNodeOutputMaterial.node: The end of a material. Whatever you connect here is what Blender shows on the object.

inputs.Surface: The shader that makes the object's look. Plug your main shader here.
inputs.Volume: A shader that fills the inside of the object, like smoke or fog.
inputs.Displacement: Moves the real surface in or out. Plug in a Displacement or Bump node.
inputs.Thickness: How thick the object counts as for subsurface and light bending. Mostly used by EEVEE. Empty uses the real shape.

ShaderNodeOutputWorld.node: The end of the World node tree. It decides the color and light of the sky and background.

inputs.Surface: The shader for the sky and background light. Usually a Background node.
inputs.Volume: A shader for fog or air that fills the whole scene.

ShaderNodeParticleInfo.node: Reads data about the particle that made this object, such as its age, size and speed.

ShaderNodePointInfo.node: Reads data about each point in a point cloud, such as its position, radius and a random value.

ShaderNodeRGB.node: A color picker. It gives out one fixed color you choose, which you can send to other nodes.

ShaderNodeRGBCurve.node: Adjusts colors with curves you draw for all channels or for red, green and blue separately. Like Curves in photo apps.

inputs.Fac: How strongly the effect is applied. 0 leaves the input unchanged; 1 applies the effect fully.
inputs.Color: The color to adjust with the curves.

ShaderNodeRGBToBW.node: Turns a color into a gray value based on how bright it looks to the eye. Use it to make a mask from a color.

inputs.Color: The color to turn into gray.

ShaderNodeRadialTiling.node: Repeats a pattern around a center like a kaleidoscope or flower, with a set number of sides.

inputs.Vector: The coordinates to pattern. Empty uses the default position.
inputs.Sides: How many slices around the center. Low gives big wedges like a triangle; high gives a fine, round pattern.
inputs.Roundness: How round the shape is. 0 has sharp straight corners; 1 is a smooth circle.

ShaderNodeRaycast.node: Shoots a ray from a point in a direction and reports what it hits. Use it for effects like contact shadows or dirt.

inputs.Position: The start point of the ray, in world space.
inputs.Direction: The direction the ray travels in.
inputs.Length: How far the ray looks. Small only finds close hits; large finds far ones.

ShaderNodeScript.node: Runs a custom OSL script as a shader. It only works in Cycles on the CPU with Open Shading Language enabled.

ShaderNodeSeparateColor.node: Splits a color into three separate numbers (like red, green, blue). Opposite of Combine Color.

inputs.Color: The color to split into three numbers.

ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ.node: Splits a vector (a point or direction) into its X, Y and Z numbers. Opposite of Combine XYZ.

inputs.Vector: The vector to split into X, Y and Z.

ShaderNodeShaderToRGB.node: Turns the final lit look of a shader into a plain color. EEVEE only. Use it for toon looks and custom shading.

inputs.Shader: The shader whose final lit look you want as a color.

ShaderNodeSqueeze.node: Old node that squishes a number with a curve around a center. Deprecated, so use Math or Map Range instead.

inputs.Width: How strong the squeeze is. Larger values squash faster away from the center.
inputs.Center: The point the squeeze happens around.

ShaderNodeSubsurfaceScattering.node: Lets light enter a surface and spread inside before leaving, like skin, wax or milk. Gives a soft, glowy look.

inputs.Color: The color of the surface seen after light scatters.
inputs.Scale: Overall size of the scattering. Small is a tight glow; large spreads light deeper.
inputs.Radius: How far light travels inside for red, green and blue. Higher in a color means that color spreads farther.
inputs.IOR: How strongly light bends at the surface. Used by the Random Walk (Skin) method only.
inputs.Roughness: Roughness of the surface reflection. Used by the Random Walk (Skin) method only.
inputs.Anisotropy: Direction light scatters inside. Negative bounces back; 0 is even; positive pushes forward.
inputs.Normal: The direction the surface faces for lighting. Plug in Bump or Normal Map for fake detail. Empty uses the real surface.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeTangent.node: Gives a direction that runs along the surface. Plug it into the Tangent input of an Anisotropic shader.

ShaderNodeTexBrick.node: Makes a brick wall pattern with two brick colors and mortar. Use it for walls, paving and tiles.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.Color1: The color of one set of bricks.
inputs.Color2: The color of the other set of bricks, mixed in to vary the wall.
inputs.Mortar: The color of the gaps between bricks.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low values make big, few shapes; high values make many tiny ones.
inputs.Mortar Size: Thickness of the gaps. 0 is no gaps; higher makes wider lines.
inputs.Mortar Smooth: Softens the edge of the gaps. 0 is sharp; 1 is a soft blend.
inputs.Bias: Balance of Color1 and Color2. -1 is mostly Color1; 1 is mostly Color2.
inputs.Brick Width: How wide each brick is compared with the default. Higher is longer bricks.
inputs.Row Height: How tall each row is compared with the default. Higher is taller bricks.

ShaderNodeTexChecker.node: Makes a checkerboard of two colors. Handy for checking how a texture is stretched.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.Color1: The color of the first squares.
inputs.Color2: The color of the other squares.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low is a few big squares; high is many tiny ones.

ShaderNodeTexCoord.node: Gives different ways to find a spot on an object, such as UV, Object, Camera or Generated. Feeds the Vector input of textures.

ShaderNodeTexEnvironment.node: Uses a 360 degree image (like an HDRI) as the world's lighting and background. Use it in the World, not on objects.

inputs.Vector: The direction to look up in the image. Empty uses the direction of each ray. Plug in Mapping to rotate the sky.

ShaderNodeTexGabor.node: Makes a wavy stripe-like noise with a direction, good for fabric, brushed metal or wood grain.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low values make big, few shapes; high values make many tiny ones.
inputs.Frequency: How tight the stripes are. Low gives wide soft waves; high gives fine thin lines.
inputs.Anisotropy: How aligned the stripes are. 0 is random directions in a blur; 1 is neat parallel stripes.
inputs.Orientation 2D: The angle of the stripes in radians. Turning it spins the stripe direction.
inputs.Orientation 3D: The direction of the stripes as a 3D vector. Used in 3D mode.

ShaderNodeTexGradient.node: Makes a smooth blend from black to white across space. Pick a shape like linear, radial or spherical.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.

ShaderNodeTexIES.node: Shapes light like a real lamp using an IES file, which stores how bright the lamp is in each direction. For Cycles lights.

inputs.Vector: The direction to look up in the lamp data. Empty uses the light direction.
inputs.Strength: How bright the light is. 0 is off; 1 is normal; higher is brighter.

ShaderNodeTexImage.node: Puts a picture on a surface. Use it for color maps, roughness maps, normal maps and more.

inputs.Vector: Where on the picture to read. Empty uses UV coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to change it.

ShaderNodeTexMagic.node: Makes a colorful, swirly pattern. Mostly used for stylized effects or as a quick random pattern.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low values make big, few shapes; high values make many tiny ones.
inputs.Distortion: How warped the pattern is. Low gives neat patterns; high makes a busy, swirly look.

ShaderNodeTexNoise.node: Makes smooth, cloudy randomness. A top choice for dirt, clouds, rust, and for bending other textures.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.W: The 4th coordinate used in 4D mode. Changing it morphs the noise over time, like an animation.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low values make big, few shapes; high values make many tiny ones.
inputs.Detail: How many layers of finer noise are added. 0 is smooth and blobby; high is crisp and rough.
inputs.Roughness: How strong the finer layers are. Low is smooth; high is rough and grainy.
inputs.Lacunarity: How much finer each layer gets. Low layers are close in size; high jumps to tiny details fast.
inputs.Offset: Shifts the noise values. Used by some fractal types. Changes contrast of the details.
inputs.Gain: Boosts the detail layers. Used by some fractal types. Higher makes more extreme contrast.
inputs.Distortion: Warps the noise by itself. 0 is plain clouds; higher makes twisted, swirly shapes.

ShaderNodeTexSky.node: Makes a realistic sky with a sun, for outdoor lighting. Use it in the World node tree.

inputs.Vector: The direction to look up in the sky. Empty uses the direction of each ray.

ShaderNodeTexVoronoi.node: Makes a pattern of cells, like cracked mud, scales or stones, based on distance to random points.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.W: The 4th coordinate used in 4D mode. Changing it morphs the cells over time.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low values make big, few shapes; high values make many tiny ones.
inputs.Detail: How many layers of finer cells are added. 0 is one layer; higher adds small details.
inputs.Roughness: How strong the finer layers are. Low is smooth; high gives strong small details.
inputs.Lacunarity: How much smaller each layer of cells gets. Higher shrinks detail layers faster.
inputs.Smoothness: Rounds the cell borders. 0 is sharp cells; 1 is soft blobs. Used by Smooth F1 only.
inputs.Exponent: Changes the distance shape. Used by Minkowski only. Low is star-like; high is boxy.
inputs.Randomness: How scattered the cell points are. 0 is a neat grid; 1 is fully random.

ShaderNodeTexWave.node: Makes stripes or rings that can be bent with noise. Use it for wood, marble and ripples.

inputs.Vector: Where on the surface to read the texture. Empty uses Generated coordinates. Plug in Texture Coordinate or Mapping to control it.
inputs.Scale: Size of the pattern. Low values make big, few shapes; high values make many tiny ones.
inputs.Distortion: How wobbly the bands are. 0 is perfect lines; higher bends them like wood grain.
inputs.Detail: How many extra layers of small noise bend the bands. 0 is none; higher adds fine detail.
inputs.Detail Scale: Size of the small noise details. Low is big wobbles; high is tiny ones.
inputs.Detail Roughness: How strong the small details are. Low is smooth; high is rough.
inputs.Phase Offset: Slides the bands along. Changing it moves the stripes or rings, good for animation.

ShaderNodeTexWhiteNoise.node: Makes pure random static, a different random number or color for each input value. No smooth blending.

inputs.Vector: A 3D or 4D position used as the seed. Each different value gives a different random result.
inputs.W: The 4th seed value used in 1D and 4D modes. Changing it gives a new random value.

ShaderNodeUVAlongStroke.node: For Freestyle lines only. Gives UV coordinates that run along the length of a drawn stroke.

ShaderNodeUVMap.node: Gets a chosen UV map from the mesh. Gives the 2D coordinates that tell a texture how to wrap the model.

ShaderNodeValToRGB.node: Turns a number from 0 to 1 into a color using a gradient you edit. Great for coloring noise and masks.

inputs.Fac: The number from 0 to 1 that picks a color from the gradient. 0 is the left end; 1 is the right end.

ShaderNodeValue.node: A single number you type in. Use it as a handy slider to control many parts of your material at once.

ShaderNodeVectorCurve.node: Reshapes the X, Y and Z parts of a vector with separate curves you draw.

inputs.Fac: How strongly the effect is applied. 0 leaves the input unchanged; 1 applies the effect fully.
inputs.Vector: The vector to reshape with the curves.

ShaderNodeVectorDisplacement.node: Moves the surface in any direction, not only along the normal, using a vector map. Plug into Material Output Displacement.

inputs.Vector: A color map storing the push direction and amount per spot, like a vector displacement map.
inputs.Midlevel: The value that means no movement. Used to shift the whole effect in or out.
inputs.Scale: Overall multiplier for the push. 0 is no movement; larger exaggerates it.

ShaderNodeVectorMath.node: Does math on vectors (points or directions), such as add, scale, dot or cross product. Pick the operation from the drop-down.

inputs.Vector: The first vector for the math operation.
inputs.Vector_001: The second vector for the math operation. Hidden for one-input operations.
inputs.Vector_002: The third vector for the math operation. Only shown for operations that need three.
inputs.Scale: A single number used by the Scale operation. Multiplies the whole vector.

ShaderNodeVectorRotate.node: Spins a vector around a center using an axis and angle, or Euler rotation. Use it to rotate textures or directions.

inputs.Vector: The point or direction to rotate.
inputs.Center: The pivot point to spin around. 0,0,0 spins around the origin.
inputs.Axis: The line the vector spins around. Used in Axis Angle mode.
inputs.Angle: How far to turn, in radians. 0 is no turn; about 3.14 is half a turn.
inputs.Rotation: How far to turn on X, Y and Z, in radians. Used in Euler mode.

ShaderNodeVectorTransform.node: Converts a vector between spaces such as World, Object and Camera. The same arrow can have different numbers in each.

inputs.Vector: The vector, point or normal to convert between spaces.

ShaderNodeVertexColor.node: Reads a color painted on the mesh's vertices, or another color attribute. Use it for hand-painted tint or masks.

ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption.node: Makes light dim as it travels through a volume, like colored smoke or tinted water. It does not glow or scatter.

inputs.Color: The color that remains after light passes through. Dark absorbs more and tints the volume.
inputs.Density: How thick the volume is. 0 is clear; low is thin haze; high is dark and solid.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeVolumeCoefficients.node: Expert volume node where you directly set how much light is absorbed, scattered and emitted per color channel.

inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.
inputs.Absorption Coefficients: How strongly each color (red, green, blue) is absorbed per distance. Higher makes that color vanish faster.
inputs.Scatter Coefficients: How strongly each color is bounced around per distance. Higher makes the volume look thicker and cloudier.
inputs.Anisotropy: Direction light scatters. Negative bounces back; 0 is even; positive keeps going forward.
inputs.IOR: Index of refraction of the particles, used in the Mie phase. Changes the glare around lights.
inputs.Backscatter: Mix of forward and backward scattering in the Fournier-Forand setting. Higher adds more back glow.
inputs.Alpha: Controls the shape of scattering in the Draine setting. Higher makes more forward-heavy scatter.
inputs.Diameter: Particle size in micrometers, for the Mie setting. Small is bluish haze; large is white cloud.
inputs.Emission Coefficients: How much glow each color adds per distance. Higher makes the volume glow brighter.

ShaderNodeVolumeInfo.node: Reads data stored in volume grids, like density, color, flame and temperature from smoke simulations or VDB files.

ShaderNodeVolumePrincipled.node: The all-in-one volume node for smoke, fire, fog and clouds. Combines scattering, absorption and glow in one place.

inputs.Color: The color of the volume. Used for scattering. White is bright fog; dark is dim smoke.
inputs.Color Attribute: Name of a volume grid that gives the color per spot. Leave empty to use the Color above.
inputs.Density: How thick the volume is. 0 is clear; low is thin haze; high is dense and opaque.
inputs.Density Attribute: Name of a volume grid that gives the density per spot, usually 'density' for smoke.
inputs.Anisotropy: Direction light scatters. Negative bounces back; 0 is even; positive keeps going forward.
inputs.Absorption Color: The color tint for light being absorbed. Used to give the volume a dark, colored look.
inputs.Emission Strength: How strongly the volume glows. 0 is none; higher is brighter, like fire.
inputs.Emission Color: The color of the glow the volume gives off.
inputs.Blackbody Intensity: How much of the temperature-based fire glow to show. 0 is none; 1 is full.
inputs.Blackbody Tint: Color tint on the fire glow. White keeps the natural color.
inputs.Temperature: Heat in Kelvin for the fire glow. Low is red-orange; high is yellow-white or blue.
inputs.Temperature Attribute: Name of a volume grid that gives temperature per spot, usually 'temperature'.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeVolumeScatter.node: Makes light bounce around inside a volume, like fog, mist or clouds. Use it to add atmosphere to a scene.

inputs.Color: The color of the scattered light. White is bright fog; colors tint it.
inputs.Density: How thick the fog is. 0 is clear; low is thin mist; high is dense and cloudy.
inputs.Anisotropy: Direction light scatters. Negative bounces back; 0 is even; positive keeps going forward.
inputs.IOR: Index of refraction of the particles, used in the Mie phase. Changes the glare around lights.
inputs.Backscatter: Mix of forward and backward scattering in the Fournier-Forand setting. Higher adds more back glow.
inputs.Alpha: Controls the shape of scattering in the Draine setting. Higher makes more forward-heavy scatter.
inputs.Diameter: Particle size in micrometers, for the Mie setting. Small is bluish haze; large is white cloud.
inputs.Weight: Hidden helper value used internally to scale this shader when it is mixed. You normally leave it alone.

ShaderNodeWavelength.node: Turns a wavelength of light in nanometers into its rainbow color. Low is violet, around 550 is green, high is red.

inputs.Wavelength: Light wavelength in nanometers. About 380 is violet, 550 green, 700 deep red.

ShaderNodeWireframe.node: Shows the edges of the mesh triangles as lines, like a see-through cage. Use it for wireframe looks.

inputs.Size: How thick the lines are. Small is thin wire; large is thick, chunky lines.
